utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Madam Registrar, good morning to you. Could you kindly call the case, please.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Good morning, Your Honours. This is case number IT-05-88-T, the Prosecutor versus Vujadin Popovic et al.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Thank you. I see all the accused are here. Defence teams are here. The exception is Mr. Bourgon. The Prosecution as yesterday, Mr. Thayer and Mr. McCloskey. The witness is already in the courtroom. No preliminaries, I take it? I hear none.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Good morning, to you sir.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Good morning.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Welcome back.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: You will only be here a short while and then you're free to go back home. So Mr. Meek, I take it, will be cross-examining you. Mr. Meek is with Mr. Ostojic defending Mr. Beara.

utterances.speaker: MR. MEEK
utterances.text: Good morning, Mr. President and Your Honours. We left quickly yesterday afternoon or I would have told you then I have no questions for this witness. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: I'm very pleased to hear that, Mr. Meek. Is the Nikolic Defence going to cross-examine -- or who, whatever the arrangement is?

utterances.speaker: MS. NIKOLIC
utterances.text: No, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: No cross-examination. But I understand Borovcanin Defence team is cross-examining you. And it is Mr. Stojanovic who you see standing about to start his cross-examination. Mr. Stojanovic, go ahead.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Good morning, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Good morning, Witness.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-127 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Good morning to you too.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: I'll put only a few questions to you, because I wish us to clarify certain points together. First, I would like us to pay attention to part of the video clip we saw yesterday. Before we begin playing the video, I ask Their Honours and you to pay attention to the person on the left-hand side of the group coming out onto the asphalt road.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, this is P02047 from 2:51:08 to 2:51:42.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Do you require the sound, Mr. Stojanovic, or not, because we are not receiving any sound.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No, Your Honour, I don't require it.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Okay. So let's proceed.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Stop.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: Sir, do you see this woman in the middle of the picture in among the people carrying the wounded man?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-127 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I do.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: You also saw her carrying water alongside this wounded person when he was coming out onto the road in a multicoloured pullover on the left-hand side of the column.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-127 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: Do you remember this woman?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-127 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I probably saw her on the meadow, but I can't be sure. I'm not sure about it.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: Do you know whether she was in the column together with you?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-127 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, as we saw her in the previous part of the clip in the same place, I assume so, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: Can you recall whether while you were in the meadow she was offering medical assistance to the people who were injured in the meadow?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-127 [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I don't recall that.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: You said a little while ago that you did see her while you were on the meadow.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-127 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Excuse me, sir. I said I thought I had seen her. It's possible I saw her, but I can't be a hundred per cent certain. In my view, these were details.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: Were there other women on the meadow giving assistance to those who were injured?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-127 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, I don't know whether they were providing assistance, but I did see some women, a small number of women, not many.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, I now wish to show the witness a document which we have marked for identification. It's 4D58. It's already in e-court. It's been translated, but the translation is not in the system yet. For this reason, we have distributed the English translation to all of you, while we have a B/C/S version for the witness. This is information provided by the Municipal Secretariat for Defence of Srebrenica dated the 1st of February, 1995. It is addressed to the District Secretariat for Defence in Tuzla by the secretary in Srebrenica, Suljo Hasanovic.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: Witness, could we please read the first sentence together where the secretary of national defence from Srebrenica is informing the District Secretariat in Tuzla that with this Municipal Secretariat for Defence 73 women volunteers are registered, assigned to military units of the army of the Republic of Bosnia-Herzegovina, which exist in the free territories of the Srebrenica municipality, and in the MUP in Srebrenica there are three women volunteers. Do you see this? The first sentence of this document.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-127 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I see it all.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: My question to you is: Do you know anything about these women who were mobilised for the needs of the army of Bosnia-Herzegovina?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-127 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Sir, Counsel, I'm not denying what this document says, but in view of the circumstances, the season of the year and so on, I knew nothing of this, and that's my reply.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you. I will not insist on this line of questioning any further, but as yesterday you mentioned that you had seen two women in camouflage uniforms in the house near the asphalt road, please tell me, are you convinced that these were two women?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-127 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I'm a hundred per cent certain of that.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: Where did you see them?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-127 [Resumed]
utterances.text: They were in the house to your right as we were passing by. There was some kind of balcony on top of the stairs.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: Was it possible that they were nurses providing medical assistance?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-127 [Resumed]
utterances.text: You mean to the Serb army or in general to the wounded Muslims? Excuse me, if you could just clarify your question.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: Well, I have been taught that medical staff have to provide assistance to anyone who is injured or wounded regardless of their religion, ethnicity and so on. So that was my question.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-127 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, it's true that that is the practice. As we know, in the army there is the red cross, and even though you're in camouflage uniform, there is insignia to show that you're medical staff. However, I didn't see any of those Serb soldiers bearing such insignia or anyone coming to the aid of our wounded.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: So you did not see whether they were nurses and whether they were providing assistance to anyone.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-127 [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: I would now like to ask you about the point in time when you arrived on the meadow. What time was it when you arrived at the asphalt road?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-127 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I wish I had had a watch to consult, but approximately about 3.00, but I can't be precise about the time.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: So that was the 13th of July, 1995, about 1500 hours; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-127 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: Could you please tell us, how late was it when you set out on the bus that you boarded on?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-127 [Resumed]
utterances.text: It was sometime between 4.00 and half past 4.00.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: Also on the 13th of July, 1995?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-127 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: Yesterday, you told us that in the meadow while you were there, according to your estimate there were some 900 to a thousand people. Do you remember that?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-127 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I do, and that's correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: For the duration of the two hours that you were there, the number of prisoners of war, was it always the same or did it change?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-127 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I can guarantee that only it could go up as other people arrived. As I could see, some other people arrived later.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: And while you were there, did that number rise significantly or not?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-127 [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, it didn't rise significantly. It rose by an insignificant number of men.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: Can we look at another video clip that we have already seen here. The number is P02047, 2:38:47 to 2:38:58. That's the time. Could you please comment this still. Is this the meadow where you were?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-127 [Resumed]
utterances.text: It is.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: On the right-hand side are these prisoners of war as you described them?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-127 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, they are.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: Do you still believe that there were some 900 to a thousand people there?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-127 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I believe that, and that's what I'm claiming.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: Do you think that this is the number that you mentioned?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-127 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: And now can we take a look at another exhibit. This is Exhibit P01579.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, this is an aerial image depicting the group of prisoners of war who were there on the 13th of July, 1995, around 1400 hours. P01579 is the exhibit that I would like displayed.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: And while this is being done, sir, maybe we can have a chat.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-127 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Go ahead.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: At the time when you came out onto the asphalt road, according to the information we received from the Prosecution this area was taken a photo of and this is the result of that. The photo was taken on the 13th of July, 1995, around 1400 hours.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can the place where the meadow and the buses are depicted be blown up just a little. Very well. That's okay.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: Can you find your bearings in this photo, and could you please point to the house that you mentioned as the place where you came out onto the asphalt?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-127 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: Can you see the asphalt road and the buses on that road?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-127 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I can.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: Can you also see the meadow and the dark group or dark spot depicting men?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-127 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I can.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: Is that the group of prisoners that you spoke about yesterday?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-127 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, it is. That's the group that I spoke about.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: Will you agree with me that the length of one bus is 12 to 13 metres?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-127 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I will.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: And can you see those buses in front of the group of people?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-127 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I can. There are several buses, not just one. I don't know which bus you're referring to.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: Will you agree with me that there are no 900 men in this group?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-127 [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. We will not agree on that.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: You still maintain --

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-127 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I still maintain. I am claiming that there were up to 1.000 men there.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: As you left that place people remained in this meadow?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-127 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: And you don't know where they were taken after that?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-127 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I would like to know, but I don't.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: We have heard the testimony of one of the survivors from the Sandici meadow who told us that he had been taken to Bratunac. Did you personally have any knowledge as to where these people had been taken to?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-127 [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I didn't have any personal knowledge. I would like to know, and I would kindly ask if you know to tell me where these people were taken. I don't know. I don't have any personal knowledge as to where they were taken.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: You don't know who took them from there, do you?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-127 [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I don't.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you very much. In any case, we will tell you what we know. Let us now look at some other things that we want to clarify.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-127 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, go ahead.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: In the Krstic case you testified as well, didn't you?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-127 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I did.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: Do you remember that at the time the Prosecutor showed you photos in which you identified some Serb soldiers who wore UN flak jackets?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-127 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: And you say that during your stay in Srebrenica you saw flak jackets on UN troops.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-127 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that's correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: You said that in the Krstic case on page 2611 and 2612, from lines 17 to line 2 on the following page. During that period of time, in 1992, 1993, and 1994, did you ever see the flak jackets as were worn by the troops of the Republika Srpska army?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-127 [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: Did you ever see flak jackets on members of the BiH army in the enclave?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-127 [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: In other words, you never saw any other flak jackets but those that were worn by the UN troops; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-127 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, it is.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: I would now like to show you a still from the video clip that we saw yesterday, and this is Exhibit 4D -- P01986. P01986. While this is being done, sir, I would kindly ask you to listen to me quoting your answers from the Krstic case.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: go through this again or we have gone through it in any case, and I think more or less you can proceed. The witness knows exactly what we are talking about and what the question was. But we need to go through this in private session.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: We are in open session, Mr. Stojanovic.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can we look at a still from the same video clip. Again this is P02047, ERN is 4417, and the time is from 2:50:14 to 2:15:17. I'm talking about three seconds of the video clip here.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: And while we are looking at the video clip, I would like to draw your attention the flak jackets. This is a still from the video clip depicting members of the DutchBat in the UN base in Potocari, and this was taken on the 11th of July, 1995. Are these the flak jackets that you had in mind and that you spoke about?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-127 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I can't see it too well.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: Can we repeat the video clip? Pay attention to the colours of the flak jackets.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: Did you see them now?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-127 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. These are the colours.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: Would you agree with me that they're not black?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-127 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I will.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: Will you agree with me that the flak jackets is multicoloured actually?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-127 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, we will agree on that.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: That there's yellow?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-127 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: Then there's dark brown -- dark green and light green and coffee colour?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-127 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, all that is correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: Or the colour of coffee for the interpretation's sake. Will we agree that there are at least four different nuances of different colours here?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-127 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: Can we now look at the video clip from P02047. We saw that video clip number yesterday. The ERN number is 4417. The time is 2:50:14 to 2:50:17. And while this is being done, may this may be an opportunity for me to correct myself, because the previous clip the time was 17:15 to 17:19 [as interpreted]. Those are the correct times. 17:50 to 17:90. And now we are looking at the part of clip from 2:50:14 to 2:50:17. Can you see this still that we saw yesterday?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-127 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: Will you agree that this soldier is wearing a flak jacket?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-127 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: Will you agree with me that the colours differ from the ones that we saw on the UN soldiers?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-127 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Not greatly, but it is possible.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: So is it possible that the flak jackets are not the same?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-127 [Resumed]
utterances.text: It is not possible, because I am very familiar with those flak jackets, and I would not claim something that I wasn't sure of.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: But will you agree with me that the colours are not the same?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-127 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I will.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I am drawing my cross-examination to an end with a couple more questions, Your Honour, if I am allowed to proceed.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: By all means, Mr. Stojanovic, and conclude.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] May I ask to go into private session for my next question because of the same problem we had just a minute ago.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes. Go into private session for a while, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Okay. We are in open session again.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: Yesterday, if you recall, you spoke about the arrival of two black cars.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-127 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: Can you tell us what direction the cars came from?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-127 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, of course I can. I can orient myself and be sure that they came from the direction of Srebrenica, because when I entered the bus, it continued in the same direction. So that would have been from the direction of Srebrenica.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: So the buses were going from Srebrenica, Kravica, Bratunac, towards Konjevic Polje?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-127 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, to put it simply, towards Tuzla.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: You are sure they were two black cars?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-127 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I am.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: And you do not know who was in them?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-127 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could we now move back into private session, and then I will conclude with my set of questions.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes. Madam Registrar, private session again, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: We are in open session. It's your turn now, Madam Fauveau, please. Madam Fauveau is representing General Miletic in this case. She will be cross-examining you now.

utterances.speaker: MS. FAUVEAU
utterances.text: [Interpretation] [No interpretation].

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: I think the interpreters have taken it for granted --

utterances.speaker: MS. FAUVEAU
utterances.text: [Interpretation] The place where you surrendered to the Serbs was a place which was formally a part of the enclave of Srebrenica. The place where you surrender, was it a part of the former enclave of Srebrenica?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-127 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I apologise, could you repeat your question? I understood it differently.

utterances.speaker: MS. FAUVEAU
utterances.text: The place where you surrendered to the Serbs, was it outside the territory of the former enclave of Srebrenica?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-127 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. FAUVEAU
utterances.text: Yesterday you mentioned a house which had already been torched when you walked past it. This house was on the territory controlled by the Serbs before the enclave fell; is that right?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-127 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I think -- yes. I think it is.

utterances.speaker: MS. FAUVEAU
utterances.text: And therefore you have no idea who was responsible for burning the house down?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-127 [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I have no idea.

utterances.speaker: MS. FAUVEAU
utterances.text: Thank you very much. I have no further questions.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-127 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Mr. Krgovic is lead counsel defending General Gvero. He will be cross-examining you now. Mr. Krgovic.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Sir, I will move a little so you can see me. I will put a few questions to you concerning the period before you set out with the column, and I will have a brief set of questions about the time when the column set out towards Tuzla. That will be the topic I will deal with.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-127 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Go ahead.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: Yesterday --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: One moment. One moment. Usher, I want to make sure that there is visual eye contact with -- between the two. If you could open up a little bit the flap. Yes, there. And I think that's safe enough as it is. Can you -- can you see each other better like that?

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, yes. We can see each other very well.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: Yesterday you said, in answer to a question, that the gathering of people took place in Kazani.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-127 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: After that you set out toward Susnjari.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-127 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: When you arrived in Susnjari, an officer of the Bosnian army tried to organise the column so that it would set out towards Tuzla.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-127 [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I don't remember that, nor do I know any officers who did that.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: 1D00055. [Interpretation] Page 2 of the document. Could the B/C/S version be shown for the witness.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Thayer.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: Your Honour, are we in private session?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: No, we are not.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: If we're not, I think we may --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: This is what I'm trying to go through this document. Let's go into private session for a short while, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: This Mountain Battalion was under the command of Ejub Golic?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-127 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that's what I found out.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: Sir, I will now go back a little. When you were gathering, you said that on that day you gathered near the petrol station at Kazani.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-127 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: I would like to have a video clip played, part of the video you saw before. That's V000 4458, and the part begins with 4:45 seconds.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Stop here, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: Is this the petrol station?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-127 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: It's some 50 metres away from the entrance to the UN base. It's right next to it.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-127 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, right next to it, a little downhill.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Please continue playing the clip.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I can't hear any sound, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Neither can I, but I was assuming that you had no problem with that. If you have a problem with that, we can start again, make sure that the sound is on. All right? So technicians, please. We need to see it again, starting from 4:45 with the sound activated, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: I still can't hear anything, but ...

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: I remember seeing this video before. Of course we've seen it several times and it did have sound. Yes. Let's try, but I know exactly where he -- why he wants the sound, because very soon we see -- we hear -- okay. I think it's coming.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I apologise, Your Honour. It was functioning before.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Mr. Krgovic, it's none of your fault, so don't despair, please. Be patient, like all Judges are.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Stop, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: So the video stopped playing at 06:19:02 and started at 04:45.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: Sir, in response to the Prosecutor's question -- questions, you said that on the day when the video was taken you were in Srebrenica, in the vicinity of that area that we just saw before. Do you recognise the area?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-127 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I do.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: Did you see this on the day?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-127 [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I didn't.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can we go on playing the video clip.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes, please, let's continue seeing the video.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: Stop here, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Do you remember having seen such scenes on that day when you were in Srebrenica in that part?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-127 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I was there once. I don't know when. But this lasted over a number of days. There were people in the UN base over a number of days.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: This was taken on the 10th.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-127 [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I can't remember that.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: Could we go to the private session now?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Certainly. Madam Registrar. One moment. One moment.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: And could you repeat your question again, please, because I think it should be --

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: Do you recognise the man in the clip?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-127 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I do. I know who this is.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: And on that date you didn't see him?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-127 [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I did not.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Thayer.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: Your Honour, just for the clarity of the record, if we could have some identification of the person, and I would just note that it's at -- it looks like 8:43:7.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes. Who is this person that you see in this clip, Witness, the one with his hands raised?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I learnt that his name was Ramiz and that he was the president of the municipality at the time, and this is the information that I have about this person.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Any further questions?

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: If I were to tell you that this is Ramiz Becirevic, the head the BiH army in Srebrenica --

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-127 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know how it functioned, believe me.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: Can you please repeat the first part of your answer, because it wasn't recorded.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-127 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that's him.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can we go on playing the video clip, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Stop, please. Your Honour, I will no longer need this video clip. I'm going to ask the witness a few questions now.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: Sir, the video clip continues, but this depicted the events on the 10th of July in Srebrenica when you were there?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-127 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: Would we agree as we watched this video that the only shells that fell and that you heard were the shells that were fired from the mortar by the gas station mortar?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-127 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I will agree with that, but we also have to agree on the time and the duration of the video clip, whether the recording covers the period from morning to dusk.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: This is a continuous period.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-127 [Resumed]
utterances.text: But the school and this place, there is a distance between the two one could say. I'm sorry that I can't agree. If there was a video clip covering the entire day of the 10th, then I would agree; but I can't agree as things stand now.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: I think he's perfectly right. I mean, he's only shown -- being shown a small part of this, which refers to minutes, a few minutes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I did not want to show the whole clip, but that is the matter of further analysis.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: But even so, when we had the gathering of all those people at the UN compound, there was also another explosion heard, which certainly wasn't the one at the petrol station. So I don't think it's fair to ask the -- that question of the witness. So let's move to something else, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Just one more question, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: Sir, in your previous testimony in the Krstic case and in the statement provided to the Prosecution, when you speak about the shelling on the 10th of July, you never mentioned this in your testimony or in the statement.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-127 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I agree with that, but the question was never put to me in that way. So if it had been put in that way I would have spoken about that.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, I have no further questions for this witness.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: I thank you, Mr. Krgovic. Mr. Haynes.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYNES
utterances.text: No, thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: I take it there is no cross-examination. Is there re-examination, Mr. Thayer?

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: No, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: So there are no questions from the Bench either, which means that your testimony finishes here. I thank you on behalf of the Trial Chamber for having come over. You will receive assistance to facilitate -- organise and facilitate your return back home, and on behalf of everyone, we wish you -- I wish you a safe journey back home.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Now, exhibits. Mr. Thayer.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour. The first exhibit the Prosecution wishes to tender is P02285, the pseudonym sheet. The second is P01583. That is a clean aerial shot of the meadow. P01584 is a photograph of the house the witness testified about. The next five -- five exhibits, Your Honour, we gave 65 ter numbers included on the exhibit list but I did not show the actual stills to the witness in order to save time. Rather, I just stopped the video clip at various points. However, for the convenience of the Court, I would offer these stills just so it helps the process. I would note that there is one still that is not included in this group and that is of the individual named -- the individual calling to the people to come out of the woods. That still is not included in this, but every other still I believe which identifies individuals he knew.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: I don't see, or correct me if I'm wrong, the still of the witness --

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: Himself.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: -- identified.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: That is correct. That is also not in this group.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: So those are exhibits --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: That's intentional. The omission is intentional.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: All right.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: That is P01970, man in the camouflage shirt. P01971, two brothers. P01973, man carrying a stretcher. P01974, this is a man in a blue shirt. P01975, the same individual as before with his back to the camera next to a Serb soldier carrying a gun. If we're looking at the exhibit list, the next still -- actually, we will not intend to tender P01986. I do not believe I questioned the witness about this specific portion. It is included, of course, in the larger video clip. The final two exhibits are PIC00033. That is the aerial of the area which the witness was kept marked by the witness. The final exhibit is PIC00034. That is another photograph or the same photograph of the house as P01584 as marked by the witness.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: All right. Any objections from any of the Defence teams? None. Yes, Mr. Stojanovic? None. So all the documents that you referred to are being so admitted and the numbers will be confirmed by the registrar. I take it 1986 you've withdrawn, you're not -- you're not tendering, no?

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: That's correct, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: All right. Defence teams. I understand that the Borovcanin team would like to tender some documents. Mr. Stojanovic.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Your Honour. We would like to tender the following: 4D58, which is the information from the Municipal Secretariat for Defence in Srebrenica dated 1st of February, 1995. Then the aerial photo of Sandici taken on the 13th of July, 1995, which was marked as 4DP01579. And bearing in mind that the Prosecution has given up on this exhibit, the Defence wants to tender the video still that was marked as 4DP01986.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour. Just to avoid any misunderstanding on page 33, line 7, we would like to have -- this has just been corrected, so I withdraw the remark. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: I was going to correct it too. So any objections from the Prosecution?

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: No objections, Your Honour. And while we're with Mr. Stojanovic, I just wanted to offer some clarification because the issue was raised during the cross-examination with respect to the references to a Prosecution witness whom was the basis for some of the questions that Mr. Stojanovic asked about the -- for example, the witness's arrest record and so forth. I did not object at that time because I believe and continue to believe that Mr. Stojanovic had a good faith basis for asking those questions, and that good faith basis is that this witness to whom Mr. Stojanovic is referring is Zoran Petrovic, the individual who took the video who was accompanying the accused Borovcanin during this period of time. We do intend to call Mr. Petrovic as a witness, and I just wanted to clarify that for the Court, so you understand what the basis was and who this witness is.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: All right. Fair enough. Fair enough, and I thank you for that information. Mr. Krgovic, no documents? Madam Fauveau neither. I think that's it. And that concludes -- yeah, they are so admitted. Obviously there is no objection from any of the Defence teams or the Prosecution. So they are so admitted. Now, I understand that the next witness has had an accident on the way to the Tribunal.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: I'm not sure it was on the way to --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: In any case, he's had an accident and he's not available.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: That's correct. Early next week we should have that person.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: So what are we going to do with the next three hours?

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: I've been trying to assemble some videotape, and so I have at least one portion of a videotape that I think is relevant, and I've mentioned to counsel, and as far as I know, there's no disagreement on it. That would be the Skorpion video. If we could go briefly into private session.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes, let's go into private session for a short time and then we'll proceed with the break.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: So I thank you for that information, Mr. McCloskey. Our intention, as you -- I'm sure you would have gathered, is that if there is a way in which we could utilise the time that we have, then we'll do our best. We'll have a 30-minute break now, because we need 30 minutes because of the redactions, during which time if it is at all possible for you to reach an agreement with the Defence on the second video, then we can also see the second video. If there are any submissions against us seeing the first video, the Skorpion one, then at least give us an indication now. Okay? So the understanding is that we see today only the relevant part that you have addressed the Trial Chamber about while we were in private session.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. President. Also, if -- if the Defence has anything based on my potential suggestion last time, something they want to clarify about a witness, Mr. Stojanovic had made a brief argument about the column, and if I can answer anyone's questions about the view of the indictment towards the column, the law we're looking at, anything like that, as you know I'm sure us lawyers could talk for a good while, if need be, if that would be of any help.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: So we'll reconvene in 30 minutes' time. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes. Mr. McCloskey, do you wish to update the Trial Chamber on any possible new developments, if at all?

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. President. In discussions with the Defence team on the other video, I think we'd prefer to keep discussions going and have that played at another time, and I think that's -- that's fine. It's only seven minutes, so it's -- wouldn't have gotten a lot of time with us. On the -- and the good news on the video that we're about to show, I've had initial discussions with the Defence and there's three other witnesses that go into material related to that video and the results of exhumations and authentications, and it looks like we're going to, well, hopefully be able to reach an agreement so those three witnesses come in in some form of stipulated agreement. So that should save a lot of time, and perhaps this will be the only time the video will have to be played. So that's the good news. Otherwise, we have this video. We're ready to play it, and it will -- we haven't had much luck with video this morning, but I've asked Ms. Stewart just to still it at one point where we will recognise, hopefully, the -- the still that I referred to before of the previous -- what the previous witness was talking about. But otherwise we'll just play it the way it is, and any information or questions related to it we'll try to work out from the stipulation.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Josse.

utterances.speaker: MR. JOSSE
utterances.text: Mr. McCloskey, Your Honour, very gallantly mention whom the Defence team -- to whom the seven-minute video referred or related to. It's us. I'm very grateful to him and the Trial Chamber for allowing us a bit more time to discuss this particular issue. I personally haven't seen it. My learned friend provided some stills of it this morning. I have had a chance to discuss it with General Gvero but some more time would be appreciated.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes, and you will have all the time that you require.

utterances.speaker: MR. JOSSE
utterances.text: Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: It's not in the style of this Trial Chamber to cut you off or to -- But anyway, Mr. McCloskey, there was the other suggestion that you made. I'm just referring to it again, because I think it's a very interesting proposition that you made to the Defence teams, namely that -- particularly when you referred to Mr. Stojanovic's argument with the column and your availability to answer anybody's questions about the review of the indictment towards the column, the law, and so on and so forth. If you can take that up further in due course, I think it will be extremely beneficial, to everyone, I would imagine. So let's go to the video. Do we need all this light for the video or can we lower it a little bit down?

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Look down in the left corner for subtitles. I haven't seen this style before, but that's where you need to look.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: That's all we have for the day, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Can we adjourn? Next sitting will be on Monday, and I think it's in the morning. It's in the morning. But then the rest of the week it's in the afternoon, and we are not sitting on Friday. That's upon the request of one of the Defence teams. All right. We stand adjourned. Thank you. Have a nice weekend. Is this tendered already or not yet?

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: No, but I can tender it.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: You can do it next time.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Okay. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: to be reconvened on Monday, the 6th day of November, 2006, at 9.00 a.m.

procedural_notes.text: --- Whereupon the hearing adjourned at 11.28 a.m.,
